analysis:
The PR is a documentation and CI-routing rescope that removes retained console-ui references. It makes no runtime provider, protocol, crypto or attestation changes.

docs/reference/provider-authorization.md: the date is bumped and the console-copy sentence is reworded to point at darkbloom-platform. The App Attest and legacy authorization semantics (TB-011, T-052..T-058, A-015..A-017) are unchanged. The text still says denied, expired or unknown grants must not become permission, that the platform owns backend policy, and that removal readiness needs fresh decisions.

docs/reference/telemetry-schema.md: the date is bumped and the TypeScript mirror row now links to immutable platform commit 48a198c. The telemetry claims are untouched: the client facade stays inert, there is no ingestion route, and fields are fixed at the call site. This introduces no new data exposure.

scripts/ci-component-paths.py: the console component, the CONSOLE patterns and the .githooks/** trigger are removed. COMPONENTS is now only provider. The classify() logic is intact and the provider patterns are untouched. Provider CI selection is unchanged; the COMMON, ci.yml and docs-skip handling is the same. Downstream workflows (.github/workflows/component-changes.yml, ci.yml) that may still read a 'console' output were not supplied. If they exist, a missing output would likely skip console jobs rather than weaken provider checks. This is a CI-coverage question, not a vulnerability. Removing .githooks/** from routing also means hook changes no longer trigger any component; this is a minor coverage change and was not verified.

scripts/docs-impact-rules.json: the console-ui telemetry-types path is dropped from the provider telemetry rule, and the 'retained console' rule is removed. This only weakens docs-drift enforcement for console files that are moving out of the repository. The 'console protocol fixtures' rule remains, so its coordinator/tests/protocol/testdata paths may be stale. That is documentation hygiene only.

No finding rests on supplied evidence. Open integration questions are whether workflow consumers of the component output and tests such as scripts/test-ci-component-paths.py were updated alongside this change. Neither was supplied.
